profile.headline: Software Engineer @ Dell
profile.summary:
I'm a Software Engineer at Dell and Computer Science graduate from Wesleyan University. With multiple years of navigating different fields in the tech industry, from video game to software and web development, my main interest and focus flow extensively. 

In every field of work, I've managed to form strong bonds with the people I work with and always assure a project gets completed with the best of my ability.

positions.description: Currently in a 3-year rotational program. Recently completed a project focused in testing automation using tools like Jenkins for end to end integration, as well as nightly regression testing.
positions.insights: Skills: Jenkins · qtest · Regression Testing · Test Automation · API Development · Python (Programming Language) · Jira

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
• Developed a full-stack application using React.js and Golang for managing and administering assets on multiple servers.
• Built 4 REST APIs to display client assets, retrieve asset details, and manage offers on various assets and servers through association/disassociation.
• Integrated the front-end UI with a back-end server to retrieve information from a Request Manager using the developed REST APIs.
• Gained experience in sprint design and demo processes, creating stories for tasks and showcasing progress bi-weekly to a team of 40+ engineers.
positions.insights: Skills: React.js · Go (Programming Language) · REST APIs · Sprint Planning · API Development · Jira · MongoDB · Software Infrastructure

positions.title: Psychology Department Web Developer
positions.description:
• Act as a liaison between the Psychology Department faculty and the web development team, understanding and translating faculty requirements into functional website features for personal, class, and research websites.
• Prioritize user experience and accessibility in all web development projects, ensuring that websites are intuitive, engaging, and accessible to a diverse audience, including students and academic peers.

positions.title: House Manager
positions.description:
• This role involves actively engaging with residents to promote academic, personal, and social development. Serve as a pivotal leader in fostering a supportive and respectful living environment, emphasizing community standards and mutual respect. Responsibilities include facilitating discussions around engagement contracts, roommate agreements, and house chores, as well as planning and implementing mission-based events and educational activities in line with Residential Life guidelines.

• Act as a first responder in emergencies, maintaining resident safety and security, and collaborating with Public Safety and Campus Fire Safety for preventive measures. Oversee the administrative aspects of residential life, including managing check-ins, closings, room changes, and participating in staff recruitment. Also responsible for maintaining effective communication with the Office of Residential Life and adhering to university policies, with a focus on upholding a high standard of conduct and serving as a role model for the student community.

positions.description:

projects.title: MessToDress
projects.description:
MessToDress is a two-player cooperative game in which you play as a cat and dog in a laundromat to clean the messy incoming clothes. Your job is to wash, dry, process, and turn in every item. Can you work together to complete as many perfect loads of laundry within a time limit? 

MessToDress was developed in 2 weeks as a prototype for the course "Videogame Architecture and Programming in Unity" at Wesleyan University. I served as the main coder throughout development, and took on animation as well.

projects.title: Conquering Monarchs
projects.description:
Conquering Monarchs is a two-player grid-based game, where each player is team King or Queen, and they place pieces (pawns, bishops, banks, and walls) on their own tiles. Players expand their territory by either placing pawns, which conquers the tile in front of where they're placed, or bishops, which allow for conquering and expanding diagonally up or down. The conquering of a tile with an enemy pawn on it destroys that enemy pawn and conquers territory. The player's objective is to protect their crown tile while attempting to capture the enemy's crown to win.

The game was completed within 3 weeks as a prototype for the "Videogame Architecture and Programming in Unity" course at Wesleyan University. I served as the main coder throughout development, and took on animation as well.
